rationale: Typed ode_system contract inherited verbatim: 2 states (T target, T_core), state_rhs, and initial conditions unchanged; only time range, fixed parameters, and noise chosen. Physical scaling: k_rad = 3*sigma_SB/(rho*c_p*r) ~ 1e-12 K^-3 s^-1 for a ~5 cm iron sphere gives ~0.5 K/s initial radiative cooling and a multi-thousand-second relaxation, so t in [0,3000] s with 300 points captures the full relaxation and the window where the new gas channel is strongest (t~2683 s). emiss_0=0.5 baseline emissivity with small positive emiss_slope; eps_selfabs=5e-13 gives an O(10-50%) self-absorption saturation over the T^4 range; h_conv/beta_buoy give a modest buoyant convective channel; C_ratio=1 with g_cond=1e-3 and T_core_wall_coupling=0.9 makes the core lag the surface and feed the coupling term. New-term parameters taken at the upper end of the suggested physical ranges (emiss_gas=0.3, gas_absorptivity=0.9, tau_gas=1e-3) so the residual-gas radiative channel is clearly excited (3710x sigma). noise=0.01 K is a small (~2-5% of initial dT_dt) visibility yardstick that keeps even the subtler saturation/buoyancy terms above 5*sigma.

scenario_text: A hot metal sphere is suspended in a large evacuated enclosure whose walls are held at a low fixed temperature, so heat leaves only by radiative exchange. The sphere's temperature falls over time as it emits thermal radiation, with the loss rate depending strongly on its current temperature. Observers track the surface temperature as it relaxes toward the enclosure temperature.
